title: telemetry-smoke-test-harness-dashboard-scaffold
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, repeatable telemetry smoke-test harness and a companion dashboard scaffold intended to validate observability fidelity for inference rollouts and bursty load scenarios. The goal is not deep long-tail investigation, but fast verification that metrics + traces behave as expected during: canaries, capacity bursts, failover/fallbacks, and model variant routing.

Why we need a dedicated smoke harness:
- Several incidents showed metric "inflation" (spikes in derived metrics) during short bursts where raw counters were fine but ratios/divisions amplified noise.
- Long dashboards are slow to parse during oncall; we need a small, deterministic set of probes that exercise common failure modes and provide a single-pass health verdict.
- Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments surface slightly different telemetry (agent vs sidecar vs in-process). A harness helps standardize acceptance checks.

Principles:
1) Lightweight: run in <60s for single probe run; full sweep <10 minutes.
2) Deterministic variants: fixed seed inputs and payload shapes to exercise prefix/KV cache, async batching, and routing fanout.
3) Incremental sampling: start sparse, escalate tracing for failed probes only to limit trace costs.
4) Minimal dashboard slice: one-page verdict with drilllinks to deeper dashboards only when failing.
5) Cross-environment parity: harness config should map 1:1 to hosted/dedicated/private probe agents.

Probe types (examples):
- Cold-start prefix probe: single request for a long-context prompt to measure TTFK (time-to-first-token), kv-warmth index, and kernel selection path.
- Burst microbatch probe: 50 small requests in parallel to trigger batching decisions and observe batching latency distribution.
- Fallback routing probe: simulate overloaded primary variant and ensure traffic reroutes to fallback variant with captured routing_reason tag.
- Prefetch/kv-eviction probe: sequence of requests that intentionally evict and re-warm kv entries to validate eviction counters and session warmth metrics.
- Embedding fanout probe: multi-model embedding request fanout to verify per-model cost attribution and trace parent-child linking.

Metric definitions (canonical smoke set):
- smoke.ttfk.p50 (ms): median TTFK for cold-start prefix probe; source = probe span ttfk measurement. Threshold: <120ms for dedicated, <250ms hosted.
- smoke.kv.warmth (0-1): ratio of hit prefixes to total prefixes in the cold-start probe session. Threshold: >0.65.
- smoke.batch.latency.p95 (ms): p95 latency across burst microbatch probe. Threshold: <400ms.
- smoke.routing.fallback.rate (%): percent of requests routed to fallback variant during induced overload. Threshold: >0 and <30%; if >30% indicates upstream overload.
- smoke.trace.trace_anchored (bool): whether probe spans include trace anchors linking request-level trace -> model-inference spans. Expect true.
- smoke.metric.stability.score (0-100): heuristic combining z-score of ratio metrics over baseline window; threshold: >70 = stable.

Trace correlation anchors (how to instrument probes):
- Every probe must emit a root span with attributes: probe.id, probe.type, probe.seed, env (hosted|dedicated|private), target_model.
- Inference spans must include: inference.kernels, sequence_length, kv_hit=true/false, routing.variant, batch.size.
- When escalating, attach operator.metadata (oncall-run-id) so traces can be grouped by smoke run.

Dashboard scaffold (single-page smoke view):
Sections (top to bottom):
1) Verdict header: green/yellow/red badge, run id, run duration, environment, and a one-line failure reason.
2) Probe summary table: row per probe, columns: probe.type, outcome (pass/fail), main_metric, observed_value, threshold, last_change_delta.
3) Compact heatmap: probe vs metric z-score; color-coded (>3 sigma red). Allows quick spotting of metric inflation.
4) Latency distribution micro-panels: TTFK p50/p95 and batch latency p95 for failing probes only.
5) Trace links: top 3 failing probe traces with direct links to trace viewer and prefilled tag filters.
6) Cost signal quick-check: synthetic cost-per-token estimation for probes to detect anomalous token accounting.
7) Operator actions (runbook quick-links): re-run probe, escalate to SRE, rollback model, disable routing fallback.

Sampling strategy and cost control:
- Default probe run: traces sampled 0.5% across the fleet, but for the smoke harness sample 100% for probe spans only, escalate to 100% for related downstream spans only when probe fails.
- Use low-cardinality tagging for probe spans (probe.type, env, model.family) to avoid trace index explosion.
- Persist probe meta-events to a lightweight event-store table (daily partition) for historical trend checks without retaining full traces.

Acceptance criteria for rollouts (how to use harness in PR gating):
- Canary passes: all probes green for 3 consecutive runs spaced 5 minutes apart OR 1 run with all pass + no regressions in the last 24h baseline.
- If smoke.metric.stability.score < 50, block rollout and require instrumentation notes.
- For quantized model rollouts, require additional kv-warmth probe to validate eviction behaviour.

Runbook (quick):
1) Kick off harness via ci/ops endpoint (or local runner with --env).
2) Wait for verdict header. If green, proceed to step 6.
3) If yellow/red: open top failing trace, confirm span anchors.
4) If metric inflation suspicion: inspect heatmap z-scores and check derived-ratio inputs counters.
5) If tracing missing: escalate to infra-instrumentation and enable targeted sampling for that run id.
6) If persistent failures across envs, block rollout and open JIRA-OPS with linked run id and top 3 traces.

Instrumentation checklist for engineering teams (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Root probe span implemented with required attributes.
- [ ] Model inference spans emit kernel selection and kv_hit flags.
- [ ] Derived metrics expose numerator/denominator raw counters for audit.
- [ ] Probe runs can be parameterized (seed, batch_size, concurrency).
- [ ] Dashboard widget consumes smoke.* metrics and heatmap source.

Implementation notes and quick snippets:
- Probe runner config (yaml) should support: concurrency, seed, target_models[], probe_timeout, tracing=true/false, env_tag.
- Minimal SQL (example) to compute z-score used in heatmap: SELECT metric, (value - AVG(value) OVER (partition)) / NULLIF(STDDEV(value) OVER (partition),0) AS z FROM probe_metrics WHERE probe_name = 'cold-start' AND ts > now() - interval '24 hours';
- Trace link template: https://traces.redwood-inference.internal/trace?run_id={{run_id}}&probe={{probe.id}}

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Where does the harness live? Option A: small service in observability repo (fast iteration). Option B: part of infra test runner (centralizes ops). Leaning to A for rapid iteration.
- Should smoke runs be automatically scheduled on every model push or gated behind feature flag? Proposal: scheduled for high-risk models and opt-in for minor rollouts.
- How long to keep probe events? Suggested 30 days for daily trends, 365 days for aggregated stability scores.

Next steps (owner + timeline):
- Asha: draft small PoC runner (observability/telemetry-harness) and run against staging models by 2025-03-10.
- Diego: dashboard mockup in Grafana and heatmap widget prototype by 2025-03-07.
- Priya: add probe span contract to instrumentation README and update model-onboarding checklist by 2025-03-05.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally minimal — focus on whether the smoke probe set gives useful early signal without high trace/metric cost. Comments on the probe list and acceptance thresholds very welcome.

Scratch ideas (future):
- "Canary fuzzing" mode where probe input perturbations randomly mutate token-level inputs to detect brittle kernel/quantization regressions.
- Lightweight probe replay: store representative short sessions to replay against new builds for deterministic regression detection.
- Dashboard "compact card" for mobile oncall view with only verdict + top failing probe.

End of doc.
